features.name: Portfolio Diversification Index
features.description: Measures cross-sectional dispersion of daily dollar-volume-adjusted returns using a rolling 20-day window. Higher values indicate greater concentration in specific stocks.
features.formula: F_t = std_dev_{i}(σ_i,t) / median(σ_i,t), where σ_i,t = rolling_std_dev(r_i,t, 20) and r_i,t = (div_adj_close_t / div_adj_close_{t-1} - 1) / portfolio_median_return_t

variables.div_adj_close_t: dividend-adjusted closing price on date t
variables.r_i,t: daily return for stock i on date t calculated as (div_adj_close_t / div_adj_close_{t-1} - 1)
variables.σ_i,t: rolling 20-day standard deviation of normalized returns for stock i on date t
variables.portfolio_median_return_t: median daily return across all stocks with valid data on date t
variables.F_t: final portfolio-level diversification index value on date t

features.normalization: Divided by portfolio median volatility to ensure scale invariance
features.interpretation: High values indicate extreme return dispersion and poor diversification; low values suggest uniform risk distribution across stocks

features.name: Market Leadership Concentration Score
features.description: Calculates the cumulative contribution of top 10% highest dollar-volume stocks to total portfolio return over 60-day window using dollar volume as liquidity proxy.
features.formula: F_t = min(1.0, sum_{i ∈ top_10%}(cum_return_i,t) / cum_return_portfolio_t), where cum_return_i,t = product_{τ=t-59}^t (div_adj_close_τ / div_adj_close_{τ-1}) and dollar_volume_i,t = div_adj_close_t * volume_t

variables.dollar_volume_i,t: daily dollar volume for stock i on date t calculated as div_adj_close_t * volume_t
variables.cum_return_i,t: 60-day cumulative return for stock i ending on date t
variables.cum_return_portfolio_t: equal-weighted 60-day cumulative return of all stocks with valid data on date t

features.normalization: Capped at 1.0 to ensure bounded output
features.interpretation: Values near 1.0 indicate performance dominated by a few large-cap stocks; lower values suggest broad-based participation

features.name: Momentum Shift Frequency
features.description: Counts the number of sign changes in rolling 20-day momentum (div_adj_close return) across all stocks on each date, normalized by total stock count.
features.formula: F_t = (count_{i}(sign(rolling_mom_i,t) ≠ sign(rolling_mom_i,t-1)) / N_t), where rolling_mom_i,t = sum_{τ=t-19}^t (div_adj_close_τ / div_adj_close_{τ-1} - 1)

variables.rolling_mom_i,t: 20-day momentum for stock i on date t calculated as sum of daily returns
variables.N_t: number of stocks with valid data on date t

features.normalization: Normalized by total number of stocks to create proportion metric
features.interpretation: High values indicate frequent momentum regime shifts; low values suggest stable directional trends

features.name: Volatility Regime Stability
features.description: Measures consistency of rolling 60-day volatility (standard deviation of div_adj_close returns) across the portfolio, normalized by median volatility.
features.formula: F_t = std_dev_{i}(vol_i,t) / median(vol_i,t), where vol_i,t = rolling_std_dev(r_i,t, 60) and r_i,t = (div_adj_close_t / div_adj_close_{t-1} - 1)

variables.r_i,t: daily return for stock i on date t calculated as (div_adj_close_t / div_adj_close_{t-1} - 1)
variables.vol_i,t: rolling 60-day standard deviation of returns for stock i on date t
variables.median(vol_i,t): median volatility across all stocks with valid data on date t

features.normalization: Divided by portfolio median volatility to ensure scale invariance
features.interpretation: High values indicate unstable volatility patterns; low values suggest consistent clustering behavior

features.name: Portfolio Regime Transition Frequency
features.description: Counts transitions between bull/bear regimes defined by cumulative div_adj_close returns over 60-day window, normalized by total stock count.
features.formula: F_t = (count_{i}(crossed_5%_threshold_i,t) / N_t), where crossed_5%_threshold_i,t = 1 if |cum_return_i,t| ≥ 0.05 and sign(cum_return_i,t) ≠ sign(cum_return_i,t-1) else 0

variables.cum_return_i,t: 60-day cumulative return for stock i ending on date t calculated as product_{τ=t-59}^t (div_adj_close_τ / div_adj_close_{τ-1})
variables.N_t: number of stocks with valid data on date t

features.normalization: Normalized by total number of stocks to create proportion metric
features.interpretation: High values indicate frequent market state transitions; low values suggest prolonged regime persistence

features.name: Systematic Risk Amplification Index
features.description: Measures correlation between individual stock returns and portfolio-wide return (internal benchmark) over rolling 60-day window.
features.formula: F_t = mean_{i}(corr(r_i,t, r_portfolio,t)), where r_portfolio,t = mean_{j}(r_j,t) and corr(x,y) = covariance(x,y)/sqrt(var(x)*var(y))

variables.r_i,t: daily return for stock i on date t calculated as (div_adj_close_t / div_adj_close_{t-1} - 1)
variables.r_portfolio,t: equal-weighted daily return of all stocks with valid data on date t

features.interpretation: High positive values indicate strong systematic risk alignment; low values suggest idiosyncratic behavior

features.name: Recovery Velocity Index
features.description: Measures time-to-recover from drawdowns using cumulative div_adj_close returns over 60-day window.
features.formula: F_t = median_{i}(days_to_recover_i,t), where days_to_recover_i,t = min(τ ≥ t-59 such that cum_return_i,τ ≥ peak_return_i,t-1)

variables.cum_return_i,t: 60-day cumulative return for stock i ending on date t calculated as product_{τ=t-59}^t (div_adj_close_τ / div_adj_close_{τ-1})
variables.peak_return_i,t-1: maximum cumulative return for stock i up to date t-1

features.interpretation: Lower values indicate faster recovery from losses; higher values suggest persistent drawdowns

features.name: Liquidity Correlation Intensity
features.description: Measures synchronization of dollar-volume changes across stocks using rolling 20-day window, normalized by median volume change volatility.
features.formula: F_t = std_dev_{i}(Δdollar_volume_i,t) / median(Δdollar_volume_i,t), where Δdollar_volume_i,t = (div_adj_close_t * volume_t - div_adj_close_{t-1} * volume_{t-1}) / (div_adj_close_{t-1} * volume_{t-1})

variables.dollar_volume_i,t: daily dollar volume for stock i on date t calculated as div_adj_close_t * volume_t
variables.Δdollar_volume_i,t: 20-day percentage change in dollar volume for stock i on date t

features.normalization: Divided by portfolio median volume change volatility to ensure scale invariance
features.interpretation: High values indicate synchronized liquidity shocks; low values suggest independent trading activity

features.name: Sentiment Coherence Score
features.description: Measures alignment between individual stock returns and portfolio-wide return (internal benchmark) over rolling 60-day window, normalized by median correlation.
features.formula: F_t = std_dev_{i}(corr(r_i,t, r_portfolio,t)) / median(corr(r_i,t, r_portfolio,t)), where corr(x,y) = covariance(x,y)/sqrt(var(x)*var(y))

variables.r_i,t: daily return for stock i on date t calculated as (div_adj_close_t / div_adj_close_{t-1} - 1)
variables.r_portfolio,t: equal-weighted daily return of all stocks with valid data on date t

features.normalization: Divided by portfolio median correlation to ensure scale invariance
features.interpretation: High values indicate divergent behavior from internal benchmark; low values suggest coherent movement

features.name: Risk Contribution Uniformity Index
features.description: Measures standard deviation of individual stock contributions to portfolio volatility over rolling 60-day window, normalized by median volatility.
features.formula: F_t = std_dev_{i}(vol_i,t) / median(vol_i,t), where vol_i,t = rolling_std_dev(r_i,t, 60) and r_i,t = (div_adj_close_t / div_adj_close_{t-1} - 1)

variables.r_i,t: daily return for stock i on date t calculated as (div_adj_close_t / div_adj_close_{t-1} - 1)
variables.vol_i,t: rolling 60-day standard deviation of returns for stock i on date t
variables.median(vol_i,t): median volatility across all stocks with valid data on date t

features.normalization: Divided by portfolio median volatility to ensure scale invariance
features.interpretation: High values indicate uneven risk distribution; low values suggest uniform contribution patterns

features.name: Portfolio Regime Adaptability Index
features.description: Measures difference in cumulative returns between high and low volatility periods over rolling 60-day window.
features.formula: F_t = (mean_{i ∈ high_vol}(cum_return_i,t) - mean_{i ∈ low_vol}(cum_return_i,t)), where high_vol = {i | vol_i,t ≥ median(vol_i,t)}, low_vol = {i | vol_i,t < median(vol_i,t)}

variables.vol_i,t: rolling 60-day standard deviation of returns for stock i on date t calculated as rolling_std_dev(r_i,t, 60)
variables.cum_return_i,t: 60-day cumulative return for stock i ending on date t calculated as product_{τ=t-59}^t (div_adj_close_τ / div_adj_close_{τ-1})

features.interpretation: High positive values indicate better performance during high volatility; negative values suggest underperformance

features.name: Information Flow Dominance Metric
features.description: Measures ratio of absolute return to dollar volume as proxy for information-driven trading activity, normalized by median ratio.
features.formula: F_t = std_dev_{i}(abs(r_i,t) / dollar_volume_i,t) / median(abs(r_i,t) / dollar_volume_i,t), where r_i,t = (div_adj_close_t / div_adj_close_{t-1} - 1) and dollar_volume_i,t = div_adj_close_t * volume_t

variables.r_i,t: daily return for stock i on date t calculated as (div_adj_close_t / div_adj_close_{t-1} - 1)
variables.dollar_volume_i,t: daily dollar volume for stock i on date t calculated as div_adj_close_t * volume_t

features.normalization: Divided by portfolio median ratio to ensure scale invariance
features.interpretation: High values indicate returns are driven more by information flow than liquidity; low values suggest noise dominance

features.name: Dynamic Correlation Stability
features.description: Measures consistency of pairwise stock correlations over rolling 60-day window, normalized by median correlation.
features.formula: F_t = std_dev_{i,j}(corr(r_i,t, r_j,t)) / median(corr(r_i,t, r_j,t)), where corr(x,y) = covariance(x,y)/sqrt(var(x)*var(y))

variables.r_i,t: daily return for stock i on date t calculated as (div_adj_close_t / div_adj_close_{t-1} - 1)

features.normalization: Divided by portfolio median correlation to ensure scale invariance
features.interpretation: High values indicate unstable inter-stock relationships; low values suggest persistent correlations

features.name: Tail Risk Exposure Concentration
features.description: Measures contribution of top 10% highest dollar-volume stocks to maximum drawdowns over rolling 60-day window.
features.formula: F_t = sum_{i ∈ top_10%}(max_drawdown_i,t) / max_drawdown_portfolio,t, where max_drawdown_i,t = (div_adj_close_min - div_adj_close_t) / div_adj_close_min and dollar_volume_i,t = div_adj_close_t * volume_t

variables.dollar_volume_i,t: daily dollar volume for stock i on date t calculated as div_adj_close_t * volume_t
variables.max_drawdown_i,t: maximum drawdown for stock i over 60-day window ending on date t

features.normalization: Normalized by portfolio maximum drawdown to ensure scale invariance
features.interpretation: High values indicate tail risk concentrated in large-cap stocks; low values suggest diversified exposure

features.name: Portfolio Entropy of Returns
features.description: Calculates Shannon entropy of daily div_adj_close returns across the portfolio over rolling 60-day window, normalized by maximum possible entropy.
features.formula: F_t = (1 / log(N_t)) * sum_{i}(p_i,t * log(p_i,t)), where p_i,t = frequency of return bins for stock i and N_t = number of stocks with valid data on date t

variables.r_i,t: daily return for stock i on date t calculated as (div_adj_close_t / div_adj_close_{t-1} - 1)
variables.p_i,t: probability distribution of returns for stock i over rolling 60-day window

features.normalization: Divided by log(N_t) to normalize entropy scale
features.interpretation: High values indicate chaotic, unpredictable return patterns; low values suggest structured behavior
